audit_question.question: Does F_append_handler_success establish the predecessor agreement required by the receiving AppendEntries boundary when an earlier request deleted a conflicting suffix but failed before refreshing cached last-log metadata? Determine whether a subsequent request can use stale metadata to obtain success, and which storage contracts and guards permit or exclude that sequence.
audit_question.importance: A local success response based on a deleted predecessor could misrepresent retained replication history. If a sender consumes that response as replication support, the mismatch could affect progress or commitment. The immediate investigation concerns the local predecessor-to-acknowledgment relation; sender-generated reachability and any decision or application consequence remain separate questions.
participants: Selected LogStore implementation and any LogCache wrapper
contexts: An earlier AppendEntries request successfully deletes a conflicting suffix and then encounters StoreLogs failure
A subsequent request names the old cached last-log index and term as its predecessor
The cached last-log index is at least the cached snapshot index, so getLastEntry selects the log cache
No intervening repair or replacement of cached history has yet been established
Concrete adapter selection and sender-generated request history remain unresolved
event_paths: Raft.appendEntries: DeleteRange succeeds -> StoreLogs fails -> return before setLastLog
Later Raft.appendEntries -> raftState.getLastEntry -> cached predecessor term comparison -> possible Success assignment
LogCache.DeleteRange invalidates its entry buffer, independently of raftState last-log metadata
counterevidence: The first request defaults to Success=false and returns immediately on StoreLogs failure; that failure is not itself a successful acknowledgment.
Older request terms and mismatched predecessor terms are rejected.
When the predecessor index differs from getLastEntry's index, the handler calls GetLog and rejects a lookup failure.
A snapshot index greater than the cached last-log index makes getLastEntry select snapshot metadata instead; this excludes some proposed stale-log cases.
Nonempty later requests may encounter GetLog failures while processing entries, preventing success even after the cached predecessor check passes.
InmemStore.StoreLogs always returns nil in the supplied implementation, so the unmodified in-memory adapter does not establish the proposed append-error prehistory.

LogCache clears its entry buffer on deletion and inserts entries only after successful backing-store writes. These protections concern its separate entry cache and do not visibly refresh raftState.lastLogIndex or lastLogTerm.
No actual execution result or evidence accompanies the existing check ID; it contributes no validation.
unknowns: The explicit RPC contract and sender interpretation of a successful response still require the requested source.

LogStore specifies inclusive deletion and error-returning writes but does not explicitly define failed-write atomicity or cross-call rollback. A concrete selected adapter's failure behavior remains unknown.

The supplied code shows the stale-cache path conditionally: successful deletion followed by StoreLogs failure returns before setLastLog, and getLastEntry can later select the unchanged pair. Whether a selected adapter and legal sender history realize those conditions remains unestablished.
Whether an ordinary sender can construct a subsequent request naming the deleted old predecessor, with entries and commit fields that permit the handler to reach success.
Whether intervening protocol processing repairs metadata, installs a snapshot, or prevents the later request from being handled.
The separate post-storage configuration-processing failure branch has not been characterized and is not being treated as equivalent to failed storage.
Whether a local acknowledgment mismatch can influence leader progress, commitment, or application remains untested.
audit_question.trigger_rationale: The acquired source resolves the cache-mechanism discriminator: raftState.getLastEntry reads cached metadata without consulting LogStore, and the handler's successful-deletion/failed-write branch does not refresh that metadata. The LogCache wrapper does not supply the missing refresh, while InmemStore does not produce the required write failure. The next reads target the acknowledgment contract and its immediate sender boundary, rather than treating this conditional source path as a confirmed violation.

selection_rationale: Continue the same Fact/establishment candidate. All five requested ranges were attached with a complete receipt; the earlier absence-of-source unknown is resolved. Source now supports a concrete conditional stale-predecessor mechanism, not merely an asymmetry. The documented getLastEntry storage representation and LogStore deletion semantics also identify a potentially checkable local relation with an independent store/snapshot oracle. Before choosing that relation or the acknowledgment relation as the obligation, the focused RPC and sender reads will establish which interpretation directly discriminates the selected question. Missing broader consequences alone will not block a subsequent bounded local check. Neither the already explained heartbeat candidate nor a separate configuration-processing failure branch offers a reason to switch questions now.
